Candidate kernel compatibility observations
==========================================

The existing test-v4l2-output-queue-module.sh gate compiles one services binary.
After that binary proves the original module's named completion failure and
the exact Builder candidate's strict queue lifecycle, it runs
TestV4L2OutputQueueCompatibility against the same loaded candidate. The existing
media job retains its decoded camera, Go2, shared-service and sample-ID consumers.
There is no additional job, module installation or binary compilation.

The new test creates its own production IPCamera node 200 only when absent, under
the existing hosted/job-owned-module admission. It uses real output MMAP buffers,
QBUF/DQBUF and capture read(2). No generated pipeline or GStreamer timer stands
in for the kernel controls. It requires all of these observations:

* Set/read back sustain_framerate and 10 fps. After one submitted frame, receive
  at least three complete identical capture frames across a 700 ms observation,
  including delivery after 200 ms, while output DQBUF remains empty/EAGAIN.
* Set/read back 400 ms timeout, fill the actual timeout_image_io buffer with a
  distinct byte pattern, submit another fresh frame, observe the timeout pattern
  only after the qualified idle interval, and recover to new submitted bytes.
  Timer delivery must not fabricate an output completion.
* Keep real writer and capture goroutines active, reopen the writer, reopen the
  reader, then release both reopen operations from one barrier. Every phase
  requires three complete frames with a new byte pattern at the expected reader
  generation. A final new pattern proves continued delivery after both reopen.

Each worker owns its descriptors/mappings. Cancellation joins both before node
removal. Unknown drain fails and retains the node for the outer guardian and
workflow cleanup. The wrapper requires every phase marker, an ordinary passing
Go test, no skipped/racy/unknown-drain output, and the absent owned node.

This is a bounded observation of those specific controls and restart sequences,
not an exhaustive V4L2 API, performance, physical-camera or firmware claim. The
runtime has a 45s guardian bound including failure cleanup; expected normal work
is a few seconds and must be measured on the hosted kernel. Local compilation
and source review cannot qualify these observations. Actual kernel execution
remains pending until the hosted compatibility.log contains all required proof.
